text: Results live on the robot: the computed calibration is written to a robot state dir (/var/lib/ros2/head_rgbd_calibration); an Apply button makes head_camera_cpp (camera_info), head_rgbd_cpp (ToF calibration) and the head URDF tof_joint use it without a redeploy (restart triggered on the robot), it survives Ansible deploys, and a Download button returns the result YAMLs so they can be committed.

Everything runs on the robot and nothing is streamed to the Mac; the operator sees live the pose count, the current status (moving / no board in RGB / board not found by the ToF: move closer / pose N captured) and the thumbnails as poses are stored.

Pose list features, all required: RGB and ToF thumbnails with the detected corners drawn; delete single poses; a coverage hint showing which image areas of RGB and ToF the stored poses cover; past sessions kept (list them, reopen any, recompute on any).

The calibration is computed on the robot from the stored poses only, without decoding bags, without running in the web_ui event loop or its 512M budget, and without starving the robot nodes (own cgroup, niced child process).

The calibration core is reused, not rebuilt: it moves into shared/ros2_common, importable from node venvs; the existing CLI keeps working on top of it; live.py, live_relay.py and capture.live are removed with a retirement test.
The IMU section, enabled on the robot in 053adfe3, keeps working on the same Calibrate page.

camera_info_file and tof_calibration_file point at the applied state files, with committed repo files only seeding an empty applied dir; docs/runbooks/head-rgbd-fusion.md steps 2-3 describe the web UI flow; the overlap with head-rgb-d-fusion-of-camera (rgbd-final-suite-and-runbook) is noted in design.md.
